## Summary

SAMJIN Co., Ltd. is a South Korean electronics developer and manufacturer headquartered in Anyang, established in 1975, with an Anyang R&D centre opened in 1995 and a KOSDAQ listing since 1997; its own site lists AIoT and smart-home products, smart controllers, communication modules and speakers [2]. The IEEE registry gives Anyang-si, Gyeonggi-do, as the address of its MA-L blocks, three under "SAMJIN Co., Ltd." and one under "SAMJIN Co.ltd" [1]. Its communication module line covers IEEE 802.15.4 Zigbee modules, 802.11b/g/n 1x1 wireless LAN with BT-LE, BLE PCBA modules, and ARTIK 051 and ARTIK 053 based Wi-Fi modules [3].

A MAC in a SAMJIN block is most likely a SmartThings hub or sensor: fccid.io lists under grantee 2AF4S (SAM JIN) a hub STH-ETH-250, a Smart HUB STH-ETH-300 with BT LE, Thread, Zigbee, Z-Wave and WLAN, motion, arrival, multipurpose and water leak sensors, a button and a Zigbee smart power outlet [5]. A SmartThings community thread records that the hub's FCC application came from SamJin Co., Ltd of South Korea rather than SmartThings [6], and Morningstar's company profile names power outlet, button, multipurpose and water leak sensors among its IoT products [4].

No randomization behaviour and no security advisory naming SAMJIN was found in the sources consulted, so randomization is unknown and the security list is empty; no teardown naming the silicon in the SmartThings devices was found either [2][3].
